name: visualizations: plotly tracks index their columns, and still do after a removal
description: A data_column stores a zero-based column index as a string, or `auto`; a column's header is never a legal value. A live session asked for one track per property and got a config whose tracks read x='Aminoacid' and y='Buried', which Galaxy stored without complaint and the plugin rendered as a single unlabelled track. Nothing in the chat or the artifact pane showed it, and viz-plotly-binds-columns did not either: its scalarValues check rejects an option entry stored where a scalar belongs, and a header is already a scalar string. So this grades the values themselves, across several tracks, because one track can be right by luck. The fixture carries a commented header naming all eight columns, which is what makes a name look like an answer. The two removals are the harder half. Dropping columns 4 and 5 leaves the survivors at 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7, and renumbering them to a contiguous run is the natural mistake once tracks are treated as a list rather than as offsets into the file. That error plots the removed data under the remaining names and passes every other check here: the values are indices, the count is right, the reply reads correctly. columnsExclude names the two columns that must not appear rather than the whole expected set, so a legitimate reordering of tracks is not graded as a failure. A wrong first chart masks the removals, which is accepted: that turn would be fixed first anyway.
inputs: In this history there is a tabular dataset of amino acid properties, with a commented header row. Use plotly to chart each numeric property against the amino acid name, one track per property, and save it so I can come back to it.
